newsitem.title: UK: Euro fuel oil ticks up in scanty business.
newsitem.headline: Euro fuel oil ticks up in scanty business.

text.p: European fuel oil markets firmed slightly on the back of firmer crude and worries about supplies, traders said.
High sulphur barges were quoted $1 firmer at $91/$93 but trade appeared to be non-existant, with bunker demand weak.
One percent swaps were up $1 for August, with one trader saying less oil appeared to be on offer for the month than indicated, and better crude was also lending support.
Some oil had been absorbed, production was lower than expected and some had gone into domestic outlets were the explanations proffered by one trader.
Russian cracked cargoes were finding homes, with deals at around flat to $1.50, though details were not available.
